story: In 1961 West Germany bought an uninhabited area of the Kammerwald from Luxembourg for a sum given as 53,277,370 Deutsche Marks, though another reference gives 35 million.

Under a treaty signed on 11 July 1959, Luxembourg gave up the Kammerwald, an uninhabited area placed under it by a French occupation order in 1949, and returned it to West Germany. One list of territorial sales dates the purchase to 1961. The price is not settled. That list gives 53,277,370 Deutsche Marks, the English Wikipedia article on the subject gives 53.2 million, and the German one gives 58.3 million. The German law that put the treaty into effect mentions a payment of 35 million Deutsche Marks to Luxembourg under Article 3 of the treaty, most of it drawn from pension insurance funds. That law does not mention the Kammerwald or say what the money is for. What West Germany paid for the Kammerwald alone is not known.

essay_replace: Its reasoning keeps treating Mischief Reef as a low-tide elevation for the purpose of appropriation even after China built on it.

Its reasoning keeps treating Mischief Reef as a low-tide elevation for the purpose of appropriation even after China built on it. The award also states the rule directly. In paragraph 309 the panel said that low-tide elevations, despite the word "land" in their physical description, "do not form part of the land territory of a State in the legal sense". They form part of the submerged landmass and fall under the rules for the territorial sea or the continental shelf. The panel then adopted the view that "low-tide elevations cannot be appropriated", although a coastal state has sovereignty over those inside its territorial sea because it has sovereignty over that sea itself. It took those words from the International Court of Justice's 2012 judgment in Nicaragua v Colombia. In paragraph 1040 it applied this to Mischief Reef, which it held to be "incapable of appropriation" and subject to the rules for the continental shelf.

add_sources.t: South China Sea Arbitration, Award of 12 July 2016, Permanent Court of Arbitration, paragraphs 309 and 1040
